description: My free English learning app aims to maximize the number of practice repetitions per unit of time while providing complete language-learning capabilities.

detailSections.title: Project
paragraphs: Czech students study English for 12 years, yet many still struggle to speak. I believe the problem is a lack of practice. Adults should be able to learn English in about a year; children may need a little longer. A few sentences per class aren’t enough. This app makes intensive practice easy, with up to 600 repetitions an hour—just one tap away.

detailSections.title: Contribution
paragraphs: So far, I’m the sole developer. I’m currently looking for an English teacher willing to create polished learning materials.

paragraphs.after: brings pronunciation, listening, vocabulary, and grammar practice together in one place.
the number of useful practice repetitions per hour, so learners can make the most of each session.
so cost does not get in the way of regular practice.
: Learners practice in both directions, English to Czech and Czech to English. This builds active recall, not just recognition.
: Learners rate how well they recalled each answer. Difficult items return more often, while familiar ones are reviewed less frequently.
: Short grammar and vocabulary lessons keep each step manageable. Overviews show what learners have practiced rather than the full amount still ahead, so beginners are not overwhelmed.
: These are the skills learners often find hardest, so the app focuses practice on understanding and speaking English.
: Learners can study whenever it suits them and choose a pace that fits their schedule.
: The PWA runs on desktop, Android, and iOS, and each action takes under 100 ms. After the initial download, it works fully offline. Personal data is stored in IndexedDB and backed up to Supabase.
: I write lessons by hand and am looking for help developing a complete curriculum. Pronunciation guides use IPA, with audio generated by eSpeak and Google Cloud Text-to-Speech.

detailSections.title: Future
paragraphs: LLM-based pronunciation feedback: I have tested it, but it is not yet good enough to justify adding it.

detailSections.title: Implementation
paragraphs: The backend uses Supabase with a PostgreSQL database and RPC functions instead of a traditional backend server.

The frontend uses Vite, React, and Tailwind CSS. The app is primarily intended as a PWA, with data stored in IndexedDB. It syncs regularly with Supabase to preserve data and remains fully functional offline.

detailSections.title: Reflection
paragraphs: I should have started with an MVP (Minimum Viable Product). As a result, refactoring took me a lot of time.
I should have progressed at a slower pace, with more focus on clean code. Some older parts of the code are hard to understand, and an AI refactor makes them only more complicated.

title: Integration Lab
imageAlt: Purple and white layered graphic representing the Integration Lab project
description: A local playground for exploring web technologies and integrations, from a React frontend and Fastify API to PostgreSQL, GraphQL, and Docker Compose.

caseStudy.overview: A local playground for experimenting with full-stack integrations across a React frontend, Fastify API, PostgreSQL database, and Docker Compose environment.
caseStudy.reflection: My original goal was to use this as a learning project and test the integration of different technologies into a full-stack application. I quickly realized that all I needed was to read the documentation and put it into practice.
